skills.name: Image generation
skills.description: Let the model generate images via Minimax (text-to-image, or image-to-image when you provide a reference URL). Tight per-turn cap because each generation costs ~1–3¢.

skills.name: File search
skills.description: Let the model pull additional sections from your attached files when their inline view was truncated. Uses Postgres full-text search over each file's full extracted text. Sign-in required — file full text is stored in Supabase.

skills.name: Web fetch
skills.description: Let the model fetch a specific URL and read its contents. Pairs naturally with Web search — search finds the page, fetch reads it in full. Per-turn cap keeps it from going wild.

skills.name: Web search
skills.description: Look up current information on the web. Picks from Tavily and Brave under the hood — toggle providers and tune their settings in this skill's panel.

envVars.description: AI Gateway (Vercel) — referenced by the `gateway` provider in config/providers.json. Required for real chat & editor AI on the default model set. When unset, the chat panel falls back to a clearly labeled mock response.

Anthropic API key — read by the Python agent service (Phase 2b-1+). When set, the executor uses the real `messages.stream` against Anthropic for any `start` job on a flagged user. Empty → the executor falls back to the Phase 2a stub step fn (two canned tokens), so the service stays runnable in dev without a live key. The Next.js side talks to Anthropic via the Vercel AI Gateway today and doesn't read this directly.

Optional Anthropic base-URL override. Empty → SDK default (https://api.anthropic.com). Set to point the Python service's `AsyncAnthropic` client at any Anthropic-compatible endpoint: - a proxy or self-hosted gateway, - a region-specific upstream (Minimax's `/anthropic/v1` host, etc.), - a local model serving the Anthropic messages API. Mirrors the TS side's `MINIMAX_CN_BASE_URL` override pattern. Has no effect when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is empty (the stub doesn't network).

Brave Search — optional. Backs the "Web search (Brave)" skill. Same fallback behaviour as Tavily when unset. Independent web index — tends to surface fresher, less SEO-spammed results. Get a key from https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com (a "Data for Search" plan is enough for chat usage). Both providers can be enabled at the same time; the model picks whichever it prefers per query and the shared per-turn cap (configurable in the right rail) applies across both.

Exa — optional. Backs the "Web search (Exa)" provider. Exa runs an embedding-based ("neural") web index that tends to surface higher- quality, link-target-style pages than keyword engines, plus an "auto" mode that picks neural vs keyword per query. Same fallback behaviour as Tavily/Brave when unset. Get a key from https://dashboard.exa.ai. All three providers can be enabled at once; results are deduped by URL and interleaved server-side, and one `webSearch` tool call counts as one cap unit regardless of how many providers it fans out to.

MCP encryption — required when any user picks Cloud-mode credentials for an MCP server. Generate with `openssl rand -base64 32`. The key lives only in the Next.js server env (AND the Python agent service env from Phase 3f-1+, which reads the same var to call the same SECURITY DEFINER decrypt RPC), never in Postgres; it's passed as an argument to the RPC at request time. Rotating invalidates existing cloud-mode creds — users have to re-add the server. Leaving unset disables cloud mode on both stacks (Local mode still works).
(no description)

Minimax-CN — referenced by the `minimax-cn` provider in config/providers.json. Optional. When BOTH vars are set, the `minimax/*` model entries in config/models.json route via the native Anthropic provider (Minimax-CN's Anthropic-compatible API) instead of going through the Vercel AI Gateway. Either var unset → minimax/* falls back to the gateway as declared by the model's `routes` list. IMPORTANT: include the `/v1` suffix in the base URL. The Anthropic SDK appends `/messages` only — it doesn't add `/v1`. So set this to the endpoint that, when `/messages` is appended, matches Minimax-CN's Anthropic-compatible POST endpoint. Example: MINIMAX_CN_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.chat/anthropic/v1 Both vars are ALSO read by the Python agent service (services/agent-py/) from Phase 3d-1+ to enable the `generateImage` tool (Minimax T2I / I2I via `/v1/image_generation`, derived from MINIMAX_CN_BASE_URL's origin). Empty MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY → the tool is omitted from the registry.

Image generation — optional. When MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY above is set, the chat route exposes a `generateImage` tool that calls Minimax's documented `/v1/image_generation` endpoint. The endpoint host is derived from MINIMAX_CN_BASE_URL's origin (image and chat share a host on Minimax — chat lives at `/anthropic/v1/messages`, image at `/v1/image_generation`). When MINIMAX_CN_BASE_URL is unset, the client falls back to the default `https://api.minimaxi.com` endpoint. Supports text-to-image and image-to-image (when the model includes a `referenceImageUrl`). Each call costs ~1–3¢ depending on aspect ratio + count, so the per-IP rate limit below defaults tight. Raise for trusted deployments behind auth; lower if you're seeing abuse.

Optional. Base URL of the Python agent service (services/agent-py/). Phase 4-2 of PLAN-agent-api.md — when set, the account menu shows a "Python agent backend" toggle that routes chat turns at `${NEXT_PUBLIC_AGENT_PY_URL}/v1/chat`. Empty (default) → the toggle is hidden and chat always uses the Next.js route. Per project policy both stacks stay live indefinitely; this is the user-facing selector, not a cutover. Example: `http://localhost:8000` in dev.

Optional. Base URL of the TypeScript agent service (services/agent-ts/). Phase 5 of PLAN-agent-ts.md — same selector wire as the Python service. When NEXT_PUBLIC_AGENT_PY_URL is also set, the account menu surfaces a 3-way segmented picker (Next.js / TS service / Python); otherwise it falls back to a single Switch. Empty (default) → no toggle, chat uses the Next.js route. Example: `http://localhost:8001` in dev.

Optional. Base URL for the backend API surface. Empty (default) means same-origin: the Next.js routes under app/api/* serve everything. Setting this to e.g. "https://api.example.com" makes lib/api-client.ts point at that host instead — used when the backend is rewritten in another language (see docs/PLAN-backend-extraction.md). NEXT_PUBLIC_* because the value is read in the browser.
(no description)

Supabase — optional. When set, users can sign in (magic link) and sync workspaces, conversations, files, and conversation assets across devices. When unset, the app runs anonymously on localStorage only.
(no description)

Ollama — optional. When OLLAMA_BASE_URL is set, the `ollama` provider in config/providers.json activates, and any model whose route uses `via: "ollama"` (e.g. `ollama/llama3.1:8b`, `ollama/qwen3:8b`) is dispatched against an OpenAI-compatible client pointed at this base URL. Typical local value: `http://localhost:11434/v1` (note the `/v1` suffix — Ollama's docs call this the "OpenAI compatibility" endpoint). OLLAMA_API_KEY is optional and usually empty — Ollama doesn't enforce auth on its OpenAI-compat endpoint. The `ollama` provider is declared with `allowInsecureBaseUrl: true` in providers.json, which (a) lets the SSRF gate accept loopback / `http://` URLs and (b) lets the route resolve without an API key. Only enable this for endpoints you fully control — by enabling it you accept that the URL is trusted not to exfiltrate any header the AI SDK may attach.

OpenRouter — optional. When OPENROUTER_API_KEY is set, the `openrouter` provider in config/providers.json activates and any model whose route uses `via: "openrouter"` is dispatched against the `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Get a key from https://openrouter.ai/keys. Two notable model entries in the default `config/models.json`: - `openrouter/auto` — OpenRouter picks the model per request based on prompt length, latency budget, and price. Lets you keep one model id in the UI while OpenRouter does the routing. - `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` (and similar) — a specific upstream model via OpenRouter's catalogue. Per-route fallback list: each non-`auto` OpenRouter entry in `config/models.json` declares a `fallbacks: [...]` array of upstream model ids. The Next.js dispatcher injects this list as `body.models` on every OpenRouter request, so when the primary upstream is overloaded / errored, OpenRouter tries the fallbacks in order without re-sending. Defaults are sensible cross-vendor (Claude ↔ GPT) — edit the file to match what your account has access to. The base URL is fixed in config/providers.json (it's not env-overridable) because OpenRouter's endpoint is hosted; there's no self-host story.

Direct Postgres connection string — server-side only. Required by the Python agent service's Phase 1+ poll loop (services/agent-py/poller.py) which needs `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` semantics that the transaction pooler doesn't expose. Use the *direct* connection from Supabase's dashboard (the one ending in `db.<project>.supabase.co:5432`), NOT the pooler (`*.pooler.supabase.com:6543`). Empty in dev → poller no-ops every tick (the service still serves /healthz + /readyz).

JWT secret — server-side only. Required by the Python agent service (services/agent-py/) for any auth-protected endpoint; without it those endpoints return 503. Find it under Project Settings → API → JWT Settings in the Supabase dashboard. The Next.js side doesn't use this directly (it reads the Supabase session cookie); only the Python service does.

Service role key — server-side only. Required for share links so the public `/share/...` pages can read the shared conversation/document via the admin client (bypasses RLS, scoped to the token-matched row only). ALSO read by the Python agent service from Phase 3d-2+ for the `generateImage` Storage-persistence path: when SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are both set, generated images get mirrored into `user-files/<user_id>/generated/...` and the model receives a long-lived signed URL instead of the short-lived Minimax URL. Without them the tool falls back to inline Minimax URLs (work for hours, then expire). Never expose to the browser.

Tavily — optional. Backs the "Web search (Tavily)" skill on the Next.js chat route AND the Python agent service's `webSearch` tool (Phase 3c of PLAN-agent-api). When unset: - Next.js side: the skill toggle still appears in the UI but the chat route omits the tool and tells the model so it falls back to training data instead of inventing a search call. - Python service: the `webSearch` tool is omitted entirely from `default_tool_registry()`, so the model never sees it.
